# Bonfire/JellyProfiles

> A third-party plugin that adds profiles to Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0. One account holds several people, each with their own watch history, library access and parental controls. It is not made by or part of Jellyfin. MIT licensed.

## Facts that are easy to get wrong

- Each profile is a real Jellyfin user, hidden from sign-in screens and linked to a main account. It has its own watch history, favourites and settings.
- Library access, rating limits and tag filters are set on the profile's Jellyfin account, so the server enforces them in every app, including apps that can't show the switcher. A profile never gets more access than its main account.
- PINs are checked on the server. Device limits are not a security boundary: an app can send any device ID.
- Profiles are created and edited from the switcher in a supported app, not from the admin dashboard.
- Install from the plugin repository `https://ahouseofbards.github.io/Bonfire-JellyProfiles/manifest.json`, then restart Jellyfin. On Docker, restart the container; the dashboard's Restart button often isn't enough.
- Full switcher: Jellyfin Web, Jellyfin for Android, Jellyfin Media Player, LG webOS 4.5 and later, and Samsung Tizen (after a one-time setup).
- Profile sign-in on the app's own screen: Jellyfin for Android TV (confirmed), Roku, Swiftfin, Findroid and Wholphin (not yet confirmed). Turn it on under Dashboard → Bonfire → TVs & Apps, and type the profile's PIN as the password.
- Apps with only a username and password box (Streamyfin, Plezy, Tsukimi) work by typing a profile's name and PIN, once the main account has signed in on that app.
- Not supported: Infuse (no Jellyfin user list) and Moonfin. The official Jellyfin apps do not add plugin support, so Bonfire can't add a switcher to them.
